newsitem.title: UK: Copper nervy in LME evening, ends lower.
newsitem.headline: Copper nervy in LME evening, ends lower.

text.p: Copper prices finished a volatile Tuesday LME trading session esconsed firmly in the minus column, with the market nervous after today's hefty sell-off, traders said.
The market managed to maintain a partial rally during late inter-office trade and closed at $1,925/1,930 a tonne, above a $1,916 low, but well down from Monday's kerb close of $2,016.
Price movements today appeared to defy fundamentals, with LME stocks falling by 13,475 tonnes to a six-year low of 132,350 tonnes.
However, there are widespread doubts that these drawdowns are due to consumption, with some traders saying inventories are just being re-located in the U.S. and, more notably, in China.
Also, there was talk that influential Canadian-based scrap metal dealer Herbie Black was selling, which knocked the market from early levels near $2,000.
Black subsequently dismissed this talk, and said he was basically flat and had no market position whatsoever.
But a nervy market slumped anyway throughout the session, with speculative liquidation breaching several chart support points before values stabilised prior to a test of $1,900.
In the short-term this level is likely to be tested, although moves will remain volatile ahead of next week's November option declarations.
